text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Companies specialising in narrow fields where they have extensive know-how were the most successful in 1997, a survey shows, pointing to construction and plant installation firms as the most profitable.
--Tel Denmark managing director Claus Jacobsen sees the likelihood of a new mobile phone price war toward the end of this year.
--By the end of 1997 some 400,000 Danes will have saved almost 80 billion crowns in investment societies.
--Young conservatives are increasingly pushing aside older, more middle-of-the road office-holders in the main opposition Liberal party.
--A poll shows that a majority of Danes believe that the government should be attacking public spending rather than trying to brake private consumption.
--Foreign investors have increased their holdings of Danish shares by 40 percent since January, to a total of 33.8 billion crowns, 2.1 billion of which is in bank stocks.
--GN Store Nord, 53.5 percent owner of telecoms operator Sonofon, says that its telecom division is expected to show dramatic growth as a result of deregulation.
--Sonofon will begin using electricity company NESA's fibre-optic cable network for its traffic this summer.
